cases.title: Vitamin B12 before and after 8 weeks of a vegan diet
cases.context: In a study looking at a plant-based diet, 11 adults switched from their usual diet to a vegan diet (a diet with no meat, fish, eggs or dairy foods) for 8 weeks and took no supplements. Serum vitamin B12 (a vitamin found mainly in animal foods) was measured in picomoles per liter (pmol/L) in a fasting blood sample before the change (measurement 1) and again after 8 weeks (measurement 2).
tasks: (i) Based on the recorded data, is there evidence that serum vitamin B12 is different before and after the 8 weeks? Assume that any quantities of interest are Normally distributed. DO NOT use R.

hypotheses.nullWords: Mean serum vitamin B12 is the same before and after the 8 weeks (the true mean after minus before difference is zero).
hypotheses.alternativeWords: Mean serum vitamin B12 is different before and after the 8 weeks (the true mean after minus before difference is not zero).

cases.symbols: \(d_i\) (difference in subject \(i\)), \(\bar d\) (mean difference), \(s_d\) (SD of the differences), \(s_{\bar d}\) (standard error of the mean difference), \(\delta\) (true mean difference), \(n\) (number of subjects), \(\nu\) (degrees of freedom).

steps.title: State the procedure and hypotheses
steps.words: Each subject is measured under both conditions, so the procedure is the paired t test on the within-subject differences. Mean serum vitamin B12 is the same before and after the 8 weeks (the true mean after minus before difference is zero). Mean serum vitamin B12 is different before and after the 8 weeks (the true mean after minus before difference is not zero).

steps.title: Form one difference per subject
steps.words: Subtract in the same direction for every subject (after minus before). The analysis now uses only these 11 numbers.

steps.title: Calculate the mean difference
steps.words: The mean difference estimates the true mean change \(\delta\) in pmol/L.

steps.title: Calculate the SD of the differences
steps.words: Square each deviation of a difference from the mean difference, add them, divide by \(n-1\), and take the square root.

steps.title: Calculate the standard error of the mean difference
steps.words: The standard error describes how much the mean difference varies from sample to sample.

steps.title: Calculate the t statistic
general: t=\frac{\bar d-\delta}{s_{\bar d}}=\frac{\bar d}{s_{\bar d}}\quad(\delta=0\text{ under }H_0)
steps.words: Under the null hypothesis the true mean difference is zero, so the numerator is the mean difference itself.

steps.title: Find the degrees of freedom and the critical value
steps.words: Open t_table.pdf, PDF page 1. Use row 10 and the two-tailed 0.05 column. The printed cutoff is 2.228.

steps.title: Make the decision and bracket P
steps.words: The magnitude of t is larger than the 0.05 cutoff, so reject the null hypothesis. In row 10 it lies between the 0.002 column (4.144) and the 0.001 column (4.587), so 0.001 < P < 0.002.

cases.conclusion: The mean change is -6.909 pmol/L, t = -4.1635 with 10 degrees of freedom. Reject the null hypothesis. There is a difference in serum vitamin B12 before and after the 8 weeks, and B12 is lower after the 8 weeks on the vegan diet (0.001 < P < 0.002).

cases.title: Newborn bilirubin by a skin meter and by the laboratory analyzer

In each of 10 newborns with jaundice, bilirubin was measured in milligrams per deciliter (mg/dL) on a heel-prick blood sample with the laboratory analyzer (measurement 1) and with the skin meter on the forehead at the same visit (measurement 2).

hypotheses.nullWords: The skin meter and the laboratory analyzer give the same mean bilirubin (the true mean meter minus laboratory difference is zero).
hypotheses.alternativeWords: The skin meter and the laboratory analyzer give different mean bilirubin values (the true mean meter minus laboratory difference is not zero).

steps.words: Each newborn is measured with both methods, so the procedure is the paired t test on the within-newborn differences. The skin meter and the laboratory analyzer give the same mean bilirubin (the true mean meter minus laboratory difference is zero). The skin meter and the laboratory analyzer give different mean bilirubin values (the true mean meter minus laboratory difference is not zero).

steps.title: Find the degrees of freedom and the critical value

steps.title: Find the degrees of freedom and the critical value
steps.words: Open t_table.pdf, PDF page 1. Use row 9 and the two-tailed 0.05 column. The printed cutoff is 2.262.

steps.title: Make the decision and bracket P
steps.words: The magnitude of t is larger than the 0.05 cutoff, so reject the null hypothesis. In row 9 it lies between the 0.01 column (3.250) and the 0.005 column (3.690), so 0.005 < P < 0.01.

steps.title: Run the same test in R
steps.words: List after first and before second so R subtracts after minus before, the same direction as the hand calculation. The full printout is shown with the code. cases.title: Calf circumference before and after a long flight, treated as two groups
cases.context: Ten passengers had calf circumference (the distance around the widest part of the lower leg) measured in centimeters (cm) with a tape measure before (measurement 1) and after (measurement 2) a 10-hour flight. The same ten passengers appear in both columns. The data are first analyzed as if the two columns came from two independent groups of ten different people.
tasks: (i) Treat the two columns as two independent groups. Based on the recorded data, is there evidence that calf circumference is different before and after the flight? Assume that any quantities of interest are Normally distributed. DO NOT use R.
(ii) The paired t test on the same data gives t = 7.787 with 9 degrees of freedom. Compare the two results and explain why the conclusions differ.

hypotheses.nullWords: Mean calf circumference is the same before and after the flight.
hypotheses.alternativeWords: Mean calf circumference is different before and after the flight.

cases.symbols: \(\bar x_i\) (group sample mean), \(s_i\) (group sample SD), \(n_i\) (group size), \(s^2\) (pooled variance), \(\nu\) (degrees of freedom).

steps.title: State the procedure and hypotheses
steps.words: The unpaired t test compares two group means as if every number came from a different person. The null hypothesis states equal population means.

steps.title: Calculate the group means and SDs
steps.words: The SDs are large because the subjects differ a lot from one another at the start.

steps.title: Pool the variances
steps.words: Each group variance is weighted by its own degrees of freedom.

steps.title: Calculate the standard error and t
steps.words: The numerator is the same mean change of 0.91 cm as in the paired analysis, but the denominator now carries the spread between subjects.

steps.title: Find the degrees of freedom and the critical value
steps.words: Open t_table.pdf, PDF page 1. Use row 18 and the two-tailed 0.05 column. The printed cutoff is 2.101.

steps.title: Make the decision
steps.words: The unpaired test does not reject the null hypothesis. In row 18 it lies between the 0.50 column (0.688) and the 0.20 column (1.330), so 0.20 < P < 0.50. The paired test on the same numbers gives t = 7.787 with 9 degrees of freedom and rejects it (P < 0.001), because pairing removes the large differences between subjects and leaves only each subject's own change.

cases.conclusion: Analyzed as two independent groups, t = 0.6982 with 18 df is below 2.101, so the unpaired test finds no difference (0.20 < P < 0.50). The paired test on the same data gives t = 7.787 with 9 df and finds an increase (P < 0.001). Ignoring the pairing hides the swelling, because the differences between passengers are much larger than each passenger's own change.

steps.words: The unpaired t test compares two group means as if every number came from a different person. The null hypothesis states equal population means.

steps.title: Calculate the group means and SDs
steps.words: The SDs are large because the subjects differ a lot from one another at the start.

steps.title: Pool the variances
steps.words: Each group variance is weighted by its own degrees of freedom.

steps.title: Calculate the standard error and t
steps.words: The numerator is the same mean change of -3.7 kg as in the paired analysis, but the denominator now carries the spread between subjects.

steps.title: Find the degrees of freedom and the critical value
steps.words: Open t_table.pdf, PDF page 1. Use row 20 and the two-tailed 0.05 column. The printed cutoff is 2.086.

cases.title: Serum creatine kinase before and after downhill walking
cases.context: In a study looking at muscle strain after exercise, 5 healthy adults walked downhill on a treadmill for 40 minutes (exercise that loads the thigh muscles while they lengthen). Serum creatine kinase (CK, an enzyme that leaks from muscle into the blood when muscle fibers are strained) was measured in units per liter (U/L) before the walk, 24 hours after the walk, and 72 hours after the walk.
tasks: Is there a difference in serum CK over time? Assume that any quantities of interest are Normally distributed. DO NOT use R. (Note: If a difference exists, do not identify which groups are different.)

hypotheses.alternative: H_A:\text{at least one treatment mean differs}
hypotheses.nullWords: Mean serum CK is the same at all three times.
hypotheses.alternativeWords: Mean serum CK is different at one or more of the three times.

cases.symbols: \(x_{ts}\) (response to treatment \(t\) in subject \(s\)), \(\bar S_s\) (subject mean), \(\bar T_t\) (treatment mean), \(\bar X\) (grand mean), \(m\) (number of treatments), \(n\) (number of subjects), \(SS\) (sum of squares), \(MS\) (mean square), \(F\) (F statistic).

steps.title: State the procedure and hypotheses
general: H_A:\text{not all treatment means are equal}
steps.words: Every subject is measured at every time, so the procedure is repeated measures ANOVA. Mean serum CK is the same at all three times.

steps.title: Calculate the subject means
steps.words: Average across the 3 treatments within each subject.

steps.title: Calculate the treatment means and the grand mean
steps.words: Average down each treatment column across the 5 subjects, then average all 15 observations.

steps.title: Calculate the sum of squares within subjects
steps.words: Each subject's own spread around their own mean is added up. Differences between subjects (SS between subjects = 107.6) are set aside.

steps.title: Calculate the treatment sum of squares
steps.words: The factor n appears because each treatment mean is based on n subjects.

steps.title: Calculate the residual sum of squares
steps.words: What remains of the within-subject variation after the treatment effect is removed is the residual.

steps.title: Calculate the mean squares and F
steps.words: A large F means the treatment means differ more than the leftover within-subject noise would explain.

steps.title: Find the critical F
steps.words: Open F_table.pdf, PDF page 1. Use numerator column \(\nu_n=2\) and denominator row \(\nu_d=8\). The lightface (P < .05) value is 4.46 and the boldface (P < .01) value is 8.65.

steps.title: Make the decision and bracket P
steps.words: F is larger than the lightface 0.05 value, so reject the null hypothesis. It is also larger than the boldface 0.01 value, so P < 0.01.

cases.conclusion: F = 80.1155 with 2 and 8 df is larger than 4.46 and also larger than the boldface 8.65. Reject the null hypothesis. There is a difference in serum CK over time (P < 0.01).

cases.title: Peak expiratory flow with four peak flow meters

tasks: Is there a difference in peak expiratory flow among the four meters? Assume that any quantities of interest are Normally distributed. DO NOT use R. (Note: If a difference exists, do not identify which groups are different.)

hypotheses.alternative: H_A:\text{at least one treatment mean differs}
hypotheses.nullWords: The mean PEF reading is the same on all four meters.
hypotheses.alternativeWords: The mean PEF reading is different on one or more of the four meters.

cases.symbols: \(x_{ts}\) (response to treatment \(t\) in subject \(s\)), \(\bar S_s\) (subject mean), \(\bar T_t\) (treatment mean), \(\bar X\) (grand mean), \(m\) (number of treatments), \(n\) (number of subjects), \(SS\) (sum of squares), \(MS\) (mean square), \(F\) (F statistic).

steps.title: State the procedure and hypotheses
general: H_A:\text{not all treatment means are equal}
steps.words: Every subject uses every meter, so the procedure is repeated measures ANOVA. The mean PEF reading is the same on all four meters.

steps.title: Calculate the subject means
steps.words: Average across the 4 treatments within each subject.

steps.title: Calculate the treatment means and the grand mean
steps.words: Average down each treatment column across the 5 subjects, then average all 20 observations.

steps.title: Calculate the sum of squares within subjects
steps.words: Each subject's own spread around their own mean is added up. Differences between subjects (SS between subjects = 35662.7) are set aside.

steps.title: Calculate the treatment sum of squares
steps.words: The factor n appears because each treatment mean is based on n subjects.

steps.title: Calculate the residual sum of squares
steps.words: What remains of the within-subject variation after the treatment effect is removed is the residual.

steps.title: Calculate the mean squares and F
steps.words: A large F means the treatment means differ more than the leftover within-subject noise would explain.

steps.title: Find the critical F
steps.words: Open F_table.pdf, PDF page 1. Use numerator column \(\nu_n=3\) and denominator row \(\nu_d=12\). The lightface (P < .05) value is 3.49 and the boldface (P < .01) value is 5.95.

steps.title: Make the decision and bracket P
steps.words: F is larger than the lightface 0.05 value, so reject the null hypothesis. It is smaller than the boldface 0.01 value, so 0.01 < P < 0.05.

cases.conclusion: F = 4.2676 with 3 and 12 df is larger than 3.49 but smaller than the boldface 5.95. Reject the null hypothesis. There is a difference in peak expiratory flow among the four meters (0.01 < P < 0.05).
cases.source: Original practice example in the course style

notes: All data are invented for practice. The raw data of every case are in its table, and check_session20.py recomputes every answer and value from those tables with NumPy/SciPy.

Differences are always measurement 2 minus measurement 1 (after minus before, meter minus laboratory, non-dominant minus dominant), as in the reference paired cases. p20-screen-tear-breakup has a negative t, so the answer is the signed t and the table comparison uses |t|.

The two s20pairedR cases store real Rscript output (R 4.6.1) in values.rOutput and values.rCode, as the reference case does. The lines are exactly as R prints them, including the leading tab before Paired t-test and the blank lines. Only blank lines at the very start and end were trimmed. The step words quote the output without colons because of the no colon rule, so the exact printed lines are the ones in values.rOutput.
The unpaired cases show the raw table (the reference unpaired case shows a summary table) so that the means, SDs and the quoted paired t can be recomputed. Their values keys match the reference case.

Outcome mix. Do not reject: p20-bilirubin-skin-meter (t = 0.790), p20-median-nerve-arms-r (t = 0.688), p20-three-bp-devices (F = 1.677), and both unpaired cases by design (the paired t on the same data rejects with P < 0.001). Close to a cutoff: p20-vegan-diet-b12 (|t| = 4.164 just above the 0.002 cutoff 4.144) and p20-screen-tear-breakup (|t| = 2.285 against 2.201). Between 0.05 and 0.01: p20-peak-flow-meters (F = 4.268 against 3.49 and 5.95).
All degrees of freedom (9, 10, 11, 18, 20 for t, and (2,8), (2,10), (3,12) for F) are printed rows, so no bracketing was needed in this session.

His own phrases are kept in context and tasks with their punctuation, for example "(Note: If a difference exists, do not identify which groups are different.)" and the Homework 3 Problem 4 asks, so tasks may contain colons. check_session20.py allows colons and semicolons in context and tasks only.
